cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in a Command ('Command Injection')

exact_cwe_mechanism.evidence: The code constructs a shell command using user input (bot parameter) with escapeshellarg(), but the exact CWE-77 mechanism requires demonstration that special elements can modify the intended command, which depends on downstream intelmqctl behavior

connection.evidence: GET parameter 'bot' flows through escapeshellarg() to $arguments, then to sprintf() with $c (sudo command), then to shell_exec()

diff_causality.evidence: The added line introduces the bot parameter into the command construction for the 'run' scope, whereas other scopes use validated id parameters

security_control.required_control: Proper command argument sanitization and validation
security_control.control_requirement_evidence: CWE-77 requires neutralization of command-injection special elements
existing_controls_checked: regex validation used for id parameter in other scopes but not for bot parameter
security_control.deficiency_evidence: escapeshellarg() is present but its effectiveness depends on downstream intelmqctl command handling; bot parameter lacks the regex validation applied to id parameters in other scopes

concrete_impact.evidence: Impact depends on whether intelmqctl properly handles escaped arguments and whether attacker can inject command modifiers

diff_counterfactual: If the candidate line were reverted, the bot parameter would not be included in the command construction for the 'run' scope, eliminating this potential injection vector.
supporting_evidence: User-controlled bot parameter flows directly to shell_exec() via command construction
escapeshellarg() is the only protection applied, unlike other scopes that use regex validation
contradicting_evidence: escapeshellarg() is properly applied to the bot parameter
The code uses filter_input() which provides some input filtering
unresolved_facts: Whether intelmqctl command properly handles escaped arguments
Whether bot parameter has any server-side validation constraints
Whether there are additional authentication/authorization checks before command execution
Whether escapeshellarg() provides sufficient protection for this specific command context
